data.why: The app has no file upload; a scientist enters pKa values and total concentration directly with sliders in the sidebar, and the app computes the Acid model and plots in-process with no external files.

goals: Build a monoprotic or polyprotic acid model from pKa values and total concentration and inspect its fractional composition (alpha) distribution across pH
Generate a pH-log c (pC) diagram for an acid system to identify the buffer regions and equivalence points
Compare how increasing the number of ionizable protons (pKa1..pKa4) changes the shape and crossing points of the distribution diagram
Explore how diluting or concentrating the acid (via the concentration slider) shifts the pC diagram
Use the interactive Plotly chart (zoom, pan, hover) to read off exact pH and fraction/concentration values at points of interest
Consult the theory page to connect the displayed diagrams to acid-base equilibrium concepts

review.summary: The tree correctly frames the app as a calculation-free way to predict acid speciation, solution pH and titration landmarks, and every one of the 14 screens I opened matches its node. It still needs fixes before filing: the '0 means unused' rule is wrong, the theory page's main readings (buffer range, linking the two diagrams, how dilution moves solution pH) are missing, and chemistry tasks are mixed with generic chart handling and explorer-only checks.
